title: E. Tokitsukaze and Beautiful Subsegments
statement:
Tokitsukaze has a permutation p of length n.

Let's call a segment [l,r] beautiful if there exist i and j satisfying p_i·p_j = max{p_l, p_{l+1}, …, p_r }, where l ≤ i < j ≤ r.

Now Tokitsukaze has q queries, in the i-th query she wants to know how many beautiful subsegments [x,y] there are in the segment [l_i,r_i] (i. e. l_i ≤ x ≤ y ≤ r_i).

The first line contains two integers n and q (1≤ n ≤ 2·10^5; 1 ≤ q ≤ 10^6) — the length of permutation p and the number of queries.

The second line contains n distinct integers p_1, p_2, …, p_n (1 ≤ p_i ≤ n) — the permutation p.

Each of the next q lines contains two integers l_i and r_i (1 ≤ l_i ≤ r_i ≤ n) — the segment [l_i,r_i] of this query.

For each query, print one integer — the numbers of beautiful subsegments in the segment [l_i,r_i].

In the first example, for the first query, there are 2 beautiful subsegments — [1,2] and [1,3].

Input:
```
8 3
1 3 5 2 4 7 6 8
1 3
1 1
1 8
```

Output:
```
2
0
10
```

Input:
```
10 10
6 1 3 2 5 8 4 10 7 9
1 8
1 10
1 2
1 4
2 4
5 8
4 10
4 7
8 10
5 9
```

Output:
```
17
25
1
5
2
0
4
1
0
0
```
